text:
PandaCode

A small, native desktop workspace for coding agents. PandaCode runs the coding
CLIs you already use — Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, OpenCode, GLM Coding
Plan, Xiaomi MiMo and Alibaba Token Plan (through Claude Code), GitHub Copilot CLI, Antigravity,
xAI's Grok Build, DeepSeek, Command Code, Cline, Kilo Code, Devin CLI, Hermes Agent and Cursor CLI (through ACP), ZCode (through its app-server protocol), Pi and its
fork omp (through Pi's RPC mode), and Meta's Muse Code (through its MSP
protocol) — side by side, with your projects, Git, a
terminal and a browser in one window.

PandaCode is free and open source under the PandaCode License, the MIT
License with one addition: forks that are used commercially or released publicly
must say "This is a fork of PandaCode" and link to this repository. There is no
account, no license key and no telemetry.

Built with Tauri 2, Rust, SQLite and plain TypeScript. It uses the operating
system's webview: no bundled Chromium, resident Node server, React runtime or
embedded editor engine.

 
 Download: 
 macOS (Apple silicon) ·
 macOS (Intel) ·
 Windows x64 ·
 Windows arm64 ·
 Linux x64 ·
 Linux arm64 ·
 All releases ·
 iPhone (TestFlight) 
 

 
 
 

 Features

 The interface

- A live scene in every thread. The conversation is a window onto one of eight
 procedural scenes (sky, alpine, aurora, dunes, lagoon, nebula, ocean, rain) that
 follows your local clock, and each thread keeps its own. In dark, light and
 imported VS Code themes. Prefer a picture? Turn on
 wallpapers in Settings → Appearance.
- One card per turn. The header shows the running step and elapsed time, the
 latest reply sits inside with Read more , and changed files open the diff from
 the footer.
- Tile up to six threads. Drag a thread from the sidebar, ⌘/Ctrl -click it or
 choose Open beside to see threads side by side. The focused tile is the full
 thread, the others update live, and ⌘⌥←/→ moves between them.
- A sidebar that sorts itself. Tasks sit in Active, Finished or Settled, plus
 Pinned, with a filter field and keyboard navigation.
- A floating action dock. Panels, Agents, Run, Deploy and task actions float over
 the thread and take no layout space.
- Three views. Conversation, Board and GitHub, from the view menu beside the
 PandaCode name.
- Quick overlay and menu bar item. A global shortcut (default ⌘/Ctrl + Shift +
 Space) opens a launcher for new and running tasks from anywhere. The menu bar item
 lists running, waiting and finished tasks with your plan usage, and Settings →
 General adds a small running agents widget.
- Find and search. ⌘/Ctrl F searches your messages and the agent's, with every
 match highlighted. The inspector's Search tab finds file names and text in files.

 Agents

- Every harness in one place. Pick the harness, model and reasoning effort
 per task; switch between them from the composer. See providers.
- Tasks and a task board. Parallel tasks across projects, a Pending → In
 progress → Review → Settled board, message queueing
 and steering while an agent runs.
- Agent teams. An architect and its workers,
 mixing harnesses and models, or named team profiles; workers run at once with no
 limit unless you set one, can start their own helpers and share a notes board. Team
 starts an automatic team; with Classic team setup on (Settings → Agents → Agent
 teams) it opens Architect & workers, where you choose the worker models and how many
 run at once. Each spawned worker is one line in the turn that started it, and the
 dock's Agents item shows them all.
- Model routing. In automatic teams (Cheap, Balanced or Best, from the Team
 button) the lead can let a local router pick each worker's model, in about 10–25 ms
 and without sending the task anywhere; a failed worker's replacement escalates to a
 stronger model. Models that keep failing pause on their own, and a failed worker
 moves to the same model on another harness. Intel Mac, x86 64 Linux and x86 64
 Windows builds route with a simpler keyword heuristic. See
 model routing.
- /btw side threads. Ask a question on the side while the agent keeps working,
 in a By the way tab that can read the main thread. See /btw.
- Schedules. You or an agent can wake a thread later, on a repeat or after another
 thread finishes. See schedules.
- Bots. Put an agent behind Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp or a local web
 chat; each conversation is an ordinary task. The sidebar's Bots view lists
 every bot with its latest message. See bots.
- Projectless chats. New chat starts a conversation with no codebase, in its
 own folder under /PandaCode Chats . See chats.
- Named connections and environment variables. Keep profiles such as "Claude Work"
 and "Claude Personal", and set global or per-agent environment variables and a custom
 executable location. See providers.
- Account pools. Pool several Claude Code or Codex accounts; when one hits its usage
 limit, the task moves to the next account and continues the same conversation. Add
 account… signs a new account in with one click in your browser. See
 account pools.
- Token saver. Per-task response-style packs that cut output tokens.
- Agent usage. Account limits and cost estimates for each installed harness
 (agent usage), and one-click CLI updates
 (agent updates).
- Skills, rules, recipes and capabilities. Settings → Tools → Skills lists every
 skill installed for any agent in one place: switch one off for a project or everywhere
 in PandaCode (agents PandaCode runs; some can only be asked not to use it), add skills
 from skills.sh, GitHub, GitLab or a local folder, and uninstall with Undo
 (skill manager). Rules are imported once in Rules & library 
 and turned on per agent (rules and library). Save multi-step
 recipes with a dry run per harness, and compare each agent's
 commands, MCP servers, hooks and skills (capabilities).
- Codex goals. /goal sets an objective with an optional token budget. See
 goals.

 Review and build

- Review every turn. Saved turn

install.title: Install
install.html:
Download the latest build from GitHub Releases:

Platform File Requirements
macOS (Apple silicon) PandaCode-macOS-arm64.dmg macOS 12+
macOS (Intel) PandaCode-macOS-x64.dmg macOS 12+
Windows x64 PandaCode-Windows-x64-setup.exe Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11
Windows arm64 PandaCode-Windows-arm64-setup.exe Windows 11 on ARM (Snapdragon X and similar)
Linux x64 PandaCode-Linux-x86_64.AppImage Ubuntu 22.04+ or compatible, X11 or XWayland
Linux arm64 PandaCode-Linux-aarch64.AppImage Ubuntu 24.04+ aarch64 or compatible, X11 or XWayland

Or from a terminal: npx pandacode downloads the latest build, verifies its update signature and installs it (on macOS it also signs the installed app locally). npx pandacode --dry-run only downloads and verifies.

With Homebrew: brew install --cask aicodeking/pandacode/pandacode on macOS, or brew install aicodeking/pandacode/pandacode on Linux (details).

The official macOS builds are Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple (verified for v0.3.103). macOS may still ask you to confirm opening a downloaded app. Signing remains optional for local and fork builds, whose ad-hoc builds need the instructions there. Windows and Linux builds are not code-signed:

  • Windows: if SmartScreen appears, click More info → Run anyway.
  • Linux: chmod +x PandaCode-Linux-x86_64.AppImage (or -aarch64), then run it. Some distributions need FUSE 2 (libfuse2), or set APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1. The AppImage runs through X11 (XWayland on Wayland) by default; if the window stays blank there, try GTK's native Wayland backend with GDK_BACKEND=wayland ./PandaCode-Linux-x86_64.AppImage.

Each file has a .sha256 checksum beside it. Once installed, PandaCode updates itself: it checks the latest release, downloads a newer version in the background, verifies its signature, and restarts to install it when no agent is working and you've stepped away (or when you click Restart to update). In Settings → About, Notify me checks but asks first (Install and restart / Later), and Off stops checking. On Linux only the AppImage updates itself; an unpacked AppImage or a package just reports new versions. See platform support for details.

Then install Git and at least one coding CLI and sign in with its normal login. PandaCode does not include provider plans or usage.

Pi installs with npm i -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; sign in through Pi's own CLI. PandaCode drives it over Pi's RPC mode and gives it PandaCode's app tools through a local loopback bridge extension. Pi has no approval system of its own, so PandaCode's extension enforces the permission modes; the integrated console needs Full access.

omp (Oh My Pi), a Pi fork that runs on Bun, installs with bun install -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent; sign in through omp itself. PandaCode drives it with the same RPC bridge as Pi and passes --approval-mode yolo so the bridge stays the only approval gate.

DeepSeek installs with npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh; PandaCode launches dsh --profile acp. An API key is optional (Settings → Agents → Providers, or DEEPSEEK_API_KEY); dsh can use its own stored credentials. With a saved key (or DEEPSEEK_API_KEY), the Usage dialog shows the account balance from api.deepseek.com.

Command Code installs with npm i -g command-code (Node 22 or newer); PandaCode launches command-code acp. Sign in once with command-code login, or save an API key in Settings → Agents → Providers (or set COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY); either one authenticates the same account. Usage limits are not shown in PandaCode; check Command Code Studio. Cline installs with npm i -g cline; PandaCode launches cline --acp. Sign in once with cline auth (or set CLINE_API_KEY); the provider and models chosen in Cline apply. See provider details.

Kilo Code installs with npm i -g @kilocode/cli; sign in with kilo auth login, then select Kilo Code in PandaCode. PandaCode launches kilo acp and uses Kilo's configured providers and models. See provider details.

Muse Code installs with Meta's launcher into ~/.local/bin/muse; run muse login once in a terminal. PandaCode launches muse serve and speaks MSP, Muse's JSON-RPC session protocol, with its sandbox and approval modes; see docs/providers.md for what each mode does and what Muse cannot express.

Antigravity runs Google's agy_acp_server, or agy acp --process-per-session through the agy CLI when that server isn't installed. See provider details.

GitHub Copilot CLI installs with npm install -g @github/copilot; run copilot login in a terminal, then select GitHub Copilot CLI in PandaCode. PandaCode launches the local copilot executable over ACP. The CLI manages its own sign-in. See provider details.

Devin CLI installs with curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash (or brew install --cask devin-cli, or the copy bundled with Devin Desktop); run devin auth login once in a terminal, then select Devin CLI in PandaCode. PandaCode launches devin acp with the CLI's own sign-in and lists every Devin model with its own thinking levels. See provider details.

ZCode installs with its install script (~/.local/bin/zcode, Node 24); run zcode once in a terminal and sign in, then select ZCode in PandaCode. PandaCode talks to zcode app-server directly — the CLI's own protocol, since it exposes no ACP mode — listing every model the account can reach with its own reasoning levels. See provider details.

Hermes Agent installs with curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash; run hermes acp --setup or configure ~/.hermes/config.yaml, then select Hermes Agent in PandaCode. PandaCode launches hermes acp and uses Hermes' configured provider and models. See provider details.

Cursor CLI installs with curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash; run agent login once in a terminal (or set CURSOR_API_KEY), then select Cursor CLI in PandaCode. PandaCode launches agent acp with the CLI's own sign-in and lists the models on your Cursor plan, each with its own thinking levels. See provider details.

Review and build
  • Review every turn. Saved turn changes with unified/split diffs, an embedded browser, and file previews. Edit a sent prompt to fork the thread from just before it.
  • Approvals at hand. Requests wait in a slim bar above the prompt, one line each, grouped with Approve all when there are several.
  • Turn checks. After a clean turn, optionally run the project's own test or check command; a failure queues one editable fix message (settings).
  • Visual progress and design canvas. A picture-in-picture timeline of annotated screenshots of what the agent is building, and HTML artboards beside the chat that you comment on element by element.
  • Run and preview. The Run button starts the project's pandacode-run.sh and opens its preview. See run project.

  • Git and worktrees. Diffs, staging, commits, per-task worktrees with a one-click local Merge into main, branch switching from the branch chip, and optional GitHub issues and pull requests through gh, including merging a task's linked pull request. Jujutsu checkouts get their own Changes panel.
  • GitHub view. Your repositories with their threads, pull requests, issues and actions; review, fix checks, merge or solve an issue in one click. Each opens as a linked thread beside the GitHub view, where you can keep chatting. See GitHub.
